scenarios.context: A girl and her father look at a backpack online.

speakerA.en: Dad, I found a good backpack online. Can we look at it together?
It's thirty dollars, and delivery is free. It has four stars from over two hundred reviews.
Most people say it's strong and comfortable. A few say the colour is different from the photo.
You can return it within fourteen days. Can I order it now?

speakerB.en: Sure. Let me see. How much is it?
That's a fair price. Let's read some of the reviews before we decide.
Then check the return policy. We should be able to send it back if we don't like it.
Yes, but I'll enter the payment details myself. Never share card information without asking me.

scenarios.context: A boy asks his mother if he can download a study app.

speakerA.en: Can I download this study app on my tablet? My teacher recommended it.
It's free, but there are some ads. There's also a paid version without them.
It asks to use my camera and contacts. Why does a study app need those?
I found another one with better reviews. It only needs storage space.

speakerB.en: Let me check first. Is it free, or do we need to pay?
Free is fine. Please read the permissions before you install it.
Good question. I don't think it needs them. Let's choose a different app.
That's much safer. Download it, and then show me how it works.

scenarios.context: A student asks a shop assistant for help with a broken phone.

speakerA.en: Hello. My phone doesn't turn on, and I don't know what happened.
I dropped it yesterday, but the screen looked fine.
Okay. How much will the repair cost if it's the battery?
That's good news. Can I pick it up this afternoon?

speakerB.en: Let me have a look. Did you drop it or get it wet?
The battery may be damaged. I'll test it. It will take about ten minutes.
A new battery is about twenty dollars. It's cheaper than buying a new phone.
Yes, come after five. I'll also give you a one-month warranty.

scenarios.context: A mother and her son talk about using the tablet too much.

speakerA.en: Alex, you've been on your tablet for three hours. That's too long.
I understand, but your eyes need a rest, and you haven't done your homework yet.
That sounds fair. What about no screens during dinner and for one hour before bed?
Let's try it for two weeks and see if it improves. Then we can talk again.

speakerB.en: But I'm not only playing. I'm also talking to my friends and watching videos.
You're right. Maybe I can use it for one hour after I finish my homework.
Hmm, I'd prefer to keep it until bedtime, but I can try. I do sleep badly sometimes.
Deal. And can we play a board game together on Saturday evening?

scenarios.context: A brother and sister talk about a strange message.

speakerA.en: Look at this message. Someone I don't know wants to be my friend online.
No. His profile has no photo, and he's asking where I live.
I thought so. Should I block him?
Okay. I'm glad I showed you before answering.

speakerB.en: Don't reply yet. Do you know who he is?
That's a warning sign. Never give personal information to strangers.
Yes, block him and report the account. Then tell Mum and Dad about it.
You did the right thing. Also, change your password and keep your account private.
